name: Boxwork vein network
science_objective: Examine networks of thin, cross-cutting filled fractures (resistant veins) in boxwork bedrock with APXS, MAHLI and ChemCam, and image a side view of the boxwork structures.
why_it_matters: Filled fractures are where groundwater left minerals behind. NASA reports calcium sulfate veins in the bedrock between ridges, which were rare higher on the mountain.
position_source: PDS PLACES localized_interp.csv v42.0, frame ROVER, sol 4618, site 118, drive 198 (planetocentric_latitude, longitude; last ROVER row before the sol 4619 image; next row is sol 4621). The same row is in localized_pos.csv, so it is a localized solution, not an interpolated one. This is where the rover was, not the surveyed position of the feature itself. Uncertainty 0.5 m is the PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A §4.4.1.2 expected accuracy of localized rover positions against the HiRISE base map; it does not include the offset between the rover and the imaged feature.

evidence.text: Blog sols 4620-4621: APXS and MAHLI investigated resistant veins, or filled fractures, at Pular and Socompa; ChemCam analysed veins at El Carrizo and Huasco.
NASA, 23 Jun 2025: bedrock between the ridges also contains calcium sulfate veins, left behind as groundwater trickled through rock cracks.
Position accuracy: localized positions have an expected accuracy of 0.5m compared to the base map (PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A, §4.4.1.2).
